hypotheses.justification: Not needed, because hu is kept. If ε ≤ 0, then mass u P ≥ 0 (the sum of nonnegative terms, using hu), so ε/2 * mass u P ≤ 0. Also 0 ≤ mass u Q by hu. So the conclusion holds trivially. If ε > 0, the existing proof applies unchanged. The case split `rcases le_or_gt ε 0` makes it a short proof. This can be dropped on its own. It can also be dropped together with hR, using the same case analysis.

Not needed. Assume ε > 0, since ε ≤ 0 is trivial as above. The sum ∑(w a - u a) is nonnegative by hle, so hloss gives ε²/4 * R ≥ 0, hence R ≥ 0. If R > 0, use the existing proof. If R = 0, then hloss forces ∑(w-u) ≤ 0, so w = u pointwise. Then mass u P = mass w P ≤ R = 0, so ε/2 * mass u P ≤ 0 ≤ mass u Q by mass_nonneg, which holds because of hu. So the statement is true without hR, and the proof is a short case split on R. This can be dropped on its own.
